column1: # Ratchet baseline for Test.Parity: corpus <TAB> check <TAB> total <TAB> passing.
# `passing` is how many checks of that kind passed when this file was written.
# The test fails when the current number is LOWER, so the later waves lower
# these numbers instead of touching the corpora. `total` must always equal the
# real number of checks, which pins the corpus files against silent truncation.
#   w2u / u2w      - the converted text against the reference
#   roundtrip      - our W->U->W->U must land where the reference lands
#   w2u-warnings   - our warning TEXTS against the exported reference texts
#   u2w-warnings   - whether we warn at all on the way back (the corpus records
#                     only a count there, and the back-conversion texts are
# Wave 2 brought w2u from 24 to 28 (jsewts) and 25 to 29 (Lingua): the
# bracketed foreign text, the escapes and the dropped line breaks now match.
# Almost every remaining warning gap is a syllable-level one ("Subjoined y not
# expected after r", "Invalid prefix consonant", "more than one ^"), i.e. the
# orthography rules of wave 3, plus "No Tibetan characters found!" from wave 4.
